Cautiously hawkish policy message (25 bp hike to 5.25–5.50% and ongoing QT) remains intact, but the SLOOS tilts the outlook more cautious via the credit channel. July 2023 SLOOS shows broad-based tightening of lending standards across CRE (construction, land development, nonfarm nonresidential, multifamily), residential real estate (GSE-eligible, jumbo, government, QM and non-QM), HELOCs, credit cards, and auto loans, with tighter terms on credit cards and auto and weaker demand for subprime mortgages. These findings corroborate—and likely amplify—the FOMC’s note that tighter credit will weigh on activity, hiring, and inflation, especially for banks with meaningful CRE exposure. While the banking system is described as sound and resilient with policy backstops, the breadth of tightening argues for a larger and potentially more persistent growth headwind than a pure macro read would suggest. Netting the tighter credit impulse against still-robust labor data, the overall tone shifts from slightly positive to slightly negative.
